ODesign.claim: Do not add review/navigation affordances unless their scope and interaction are consistent with the user's mental model.
ODesign.conditions: Section-local answer summaries looked interactive and behaved inconsistently across page structures.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The feature did not meet the assumed need and created confusion.

ODesign.claim: Removal is a testable design intervention; validate it with a stated hypothesis and multiple guardrail metrics.
ODesign.conditions: The team did not know whether removing smart answers would harm completion.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live-service before/after measurement.

ODesign.claim: Place review at the natural commitment boundary and allow correction before submission.
ODesign.conditions: Users expected to review the whole application rather than section-local summaries.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Prototype testing plus satisfaction-survey feedback.

ODesign.claim: Optional questions are not free: each adds interpretation and decision cost.
ODesign.conditions: A form presented many optional fields without a clear information hierarchy.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Users understood and completed the section faster.

ODesign.claim: A smaller, explicit question set can improve both user effort and downstream operational quality.
ODesign.conditions: The education section was slow and confusing.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live completion-time and processing-quality data.

ODesign.claim: Flow polish cannot compensate for an intrinsically burdensome information demand.
ODesign.conditions: Employment questions added about 14 minutes and required hard-to-retrieve dates and payslips.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Completion time stayed the same; only the number of steps decreased slightly.

ODesign.claim: Escalate unresolved UX friction to policy, data, and operational-process redesign.
ODesign.conditions: A presentational redesign failed to reduce completion time.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Re-test completion time, abandonment, data completeness, and manual follow-up after implementation.

ODesign.claim: Support discoverability and support routing must be designed as one end-to-end service.
ODesign.conditions: A helpline was behind a disclosure and pointed to technical support although users needed eligibility help.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Calls were transferred because the support destination did not match the user need.

ODesign.claim: Do not equate shipping help content with a successful outcome; retain an inconclusive or failed result until metrics improve.
ODesign.conditions: The team introduced contextual links and a help guide.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Post-release completion-rate monitoring.

ODesign.claim: A good service distinguishes successful completion from a correct early exit.
ODesign.conditions: Users told they might not be entitled could only continue into a lengthy application.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Measure reason-coded exits separately from harmful abandonment.

ODesign.claim: Progress UI must answer a demonstrated question and match expected interaction.
ODesign.conditions: Users either did not notice the indicator or expected it to support navigation; some were intimidated by the section count.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Completion and time were unchanged.

ODesign.claim: A simpler system with fewer misleading components can be a successful design outcome.
ODesign.conditions: A progress component consumed attention without meeting the user need.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live guardrail metrics and follow-up feedback.

ODesign.claim: Safety-critical continuous controls require immediate, perceivable state and mode feedback; visual-only controls may be inadequate.
ODesign.conditions: Ship thrust was controlled through touch-screen throttles that could be independently ganged or unganged.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The interface increased the likelihood of operator errors contributing to a fatal collision.

ODesign.claim: Transfer of authority must be explicit, acknowledged, visible to all affected operators, and reversible.
ODesign.conditions: In backup manual mode another station could take steering without acknowledgement.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Control and mode changed in less than a second while operators perceived a system malfunction.

ODesign.claim: Match the control modality to the physical continuity, risk, and feedback needs of the task.
ODesign.conditions: Touch controls provided less direction, force, and gang-state feedback than mechanical throttles.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Conformance to ASTM F1166 plus representative bridge simulation.

ODesign.claim: A UI is not operationally complete until procedures and training cover normal, transfer, exception, and recovery states.
ODesign.conditions: Written procedures omitted transfer and ganging steps, and training had no standard for them.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Procedure traceability and observed proficiency tests.

ODesign.claim: Validation needs layered methods and performance evidence, not checklist-only approval.
ODesign.conditions: A single heuristic review cannot prove safe performance.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The published EUP protocol itself specifies the independent validation method.

ODesign.claim: Workarounds are evidence of a system-work mismatch and should trigger root-cause analysis, not normalization.
ODesign.conditions: EHR workflows did not adequately support clinical cognitive work and flexible task sequencing.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Information quality, workload, and patient-safety risks increased.

ODesign.claim: Derive functions from observed goals, coordination, variability, and workload rather than from database structure.
ODesign.conditions: Billing-centred EHR design conflicted with clinician-centred goals.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: SME correction, interdisciplinary review, iterative diagrams, and published-evidence convergence.

ODesign.claim: Pair quantitative behaviour with qualitative explanation before prioritising UX changes.
ODesign.conditions: Analytics showed what visitors did but not why.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Cross-source convergence and post-change metric monitoring.

ODesign.claim: Accessibility validation must include representative users and their actual assistive technologies.
ODesign.conditions: Conformance checks alone did not reveal lived navigation problems.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Participant study with disability-community partnership.

ODesign.claim: Launch is a measurement point; sustained success requires an evidence-backed improvement backlog.
ODesign.conditions: USA.gov and USAGov en Español needed improved discoverability and task coverage.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Usability tests, visitor feedback, click data, and outcome trends.

ODesign.claim: Multilingual UX requires managed terminology, content governance, testing, and support—not literal string substitution.
ODesign.conditions: English-only or ad-hoc translation limited access and created inconsistent support.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Language-specific content review and representative-user task testing.

ODesign.claim: Treat the design system as a governed product with research, accessibility, release notes, and contribution loops.
ODesign.conditions: Service teams otherwise recreate common components and repeat solved accessibility work.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Component research, accessibility testing, versioned releases, and cross-service adoption evidence.

ODesign.claim: For civic and high-stakes systems, certify observable task performance across diverse users rather than visual conformance alone.
ODesign.conditions: General or low-level design prescriptions did not reliably prevent voter errors or exclusion.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Qualification/certification testing against complete user-related functional requirements.

ODesign.claim: Model the full service and its support ecosystem before optimising a single interface.
ODesign.conditions: Claimant needs and service operations cross digital and assisted channels.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: End-to-end journey and operational-service assessment.

ODesign.claim: Scale validation fidelity, scenario realism, and independence with consequence severity.
ODesign.conditions: Method selection can under-test complex or safety-critical work.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Risk-based selection of observation, walkthrough, simulation, expert review, and summative tests.

ODesign.claim: The proposed AI capability solves a demonstrated need better than the baseline.
ODesign.conditions: Before selecting an AI feature or drawing a screen
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: A visually attractive AI feature is built without a validated user problem.

ODesign.claim: Optimization improves the user outcome without breaching guardrails.
ODesign.conditions: When defining AI success
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The system maximizes clicks, speed, or model score while degrading trust, safety, or task completion.

ODesign.claim: The corpus grows by distinct reusable knowledge rather than paraphrase volume.
ODesign.conditions: Before registering generated UI/UX knowledge
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Requested counts are met by changing labels, roles, or proficiency levels.

ODesign.claim: The declared scope reaches an evidenced saturation point.
ODesign.conditions: Before declaring UI/UX research complete
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Research stops when an arbitrary target count is reached.

ODesign.claim: Registered, validated, promoted, and merged counts are equal for the promoted set.
ODesign.conditions: Before moving candidate UI/UX knowledge into the official corpus
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Candidate creation or local validation is reported as learning completion.

ODesign.claim: Explore problems and alternatives broadly before converging on a defined brief and validated delivery.
ODesign.conditions: Design tasks with uncertain framing or multiple plausible solutions.
ODesign.exceptions: The framework page states CC BY 4.0; verify exact reused assets separately.
counterexamples: The first plausible result is accepted without discovery or alternative comparison.

ODesign.claim: Ground decisions in users, tasks, environments, and iterative evaluation throughout the lifecycle.
ODesign.conditions: Interactive products, services, controls, displays, and web experiences.
ODesign.exceptions: The full standard is licensed and must not be copied without rights.
counterexamples: Aesthetic preference substitutes for observed context and measured usability.

ODesign.claim: Size, contrast, spacing, alignment, and typography must express priority and reading order rather than decorate.
ODesign.conditions: Interfaces, advertisements, reports, packaging, signage, and publications.
ODesign.exceptions: Retain attribution and verify page terms before redistribution.
counterexamples: Every element competes equally or color alone carries meaning.

ODesign.claim: Physical-product design must jointly resolve appearance, functionality, manufacturability, and lasting user value.
ODesign.conditions: Mass-produced devices, appliances, tools, furniture, packaging, and controls.
procedure: Validate safety, manufacture, maintenance, and end-of-life
ODesign.exceptions: Do not reproduce protected imagery or extended source text.
counterexamples: A concept render is accepted despite unsafe ergonomics or no manufacturing route.

ODesign.claim: Physical controls, displays, sound, haptics, and companion interfaces must share one consistent state machine.
ODesign.conditions: Appliances, vehicles, kiosks, wearables, instruments, and connected products.
ODesign.exceptions: Derived candidate requiring expert validation and licensed-standard review.
counterexamples: The display contradicts the physical control or provides no recoverable feedback.

ODesign.claim: Web design must preserve perceivability, operability, understandability, and robustness as testable requirements.
ODesign.conditions: Web pages, applications, interactive documents, and embedded web views.
procedure: Meet contrast, target-size, input, and reflow rules
ODesign.exceptions: Preserve the standard version and exact criterion locator.
counterexamples: A polished page is promoted while keyboard, reflow, focus, alternatives, or target size fails.

ODesign.claim: Objective advertising claims and comparisons require documentary evidence and visible, understandable qualifications.
ODesign.conditions: Display, print, video, social, landing-page, environmental, and comparative advertising.
ODesign.exceptions: Market-specific legal review remains required.
counterexamples: Headline, imagery, or disclaimer creates a stronger promise than evidence supports.

ODesign.claim: Publication layout must preserve headings, reading order, alternatives, table structure, language, metadata, and reflow.
ODesign.conditions: Reports, books, manuals, brochures, PDF, EPUB, and digital publications.
procedure: Test tags, alternatives, zoom, and reflow
ODesign.exceptions: Evaluate each technique against target format and WCAG version.
counterexamples: The page looks correct but is flattened or has broken reading order and tables.

ODesign.claim: Typography must be tested for audience, medium, distance, language, line length, spacing, and reading duration.
ODesign.conditions: Long-form print and digital publications, manuals, reports, and captions.
ODesign.exceptions: Print-specific claims require separate evidence.
counterexamples: A fashionable treatment reduces legibility, loses characters, or breaks on export.

ODesign.claim: Generative design should create an editable foundation, preserve human control, and support repeated refinement.
ODesign.conditions: Prompt-to-layout, prompt-to-prototype, prompt-to-code, and AI asset generation.
procedure: Expose layers, components, code, and tokens
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor philosophy is descriptive, not independent proof of quality.
counterexamples: The result is a flattened image or opaque code that cannot be safely refined.

ODesign.claim: Learn general design patterns and tool structure without retaining or reproducing customer-specific content, concepts, or sensitive data.
ODesign.conditions: Training, fine-tuning, retrieval, telemetry, and prompt-to-design services.
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor statements require independent technical verification.
counterexamples: Customer designs or ideas are reproduced across tenants or reused beyond declared purposes.

ODesign.claim: Generated assets require source-rights controls, prompt and output safeguards, and provenance transparency before commercial use.
ODesign.conditions: Image, illustration, texture, advertising, packaging, brand, and publication generation.
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor claims do not replace project-specific rights review.
counterexamples: A suitable-looking asset is treated as commercially safe without rights or similarity checks.
